reuse.why: Reuses extractTagsFromText, getSheetValue, setBudget, batchMessages and the undoable/mutator wiring, but adds no shared category-selection function, so each month-wide action keeps re-deriving which categories to fill.

duplication.why: The same SELECT with group-notes join, visibility filter and template-source exclusion is pasted into setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg, followed by the same fixed-group and income/tracking skip block, and copyPreviousMonth re-states the rules a sixth way in JS.

placement.why: All logic stays in server/budget/actions.ts and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts next to its siblings, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the budget actions, their registration and tests, though setZero's query is rewritten from v_categories to raw tables along the way.

maintainability.why: Every future exclusion rule must be edited in six places in two different forms (SQL vs JS), and the step-4 flag already missed copyPreviousMonth, showing the drift this design invites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth applies hidden/template/fixed rules in JS via getBudgetData and ignores visibleCategoriesFilter and includeHiddenCategories; the five SQL-based actions inline the template-source exclusion instead of a shared selector

disguised_duplication.where: the exclusion rules are split into a SQL fragment (visibleCategoriesFilter + inline template_settings clause) repeated in five queries and a reshaped JS version in copyPreviousMonth (template_source === 'ui', hidden/group_hidden checks)

abstraction_drift.where: includeHiddenCategories threaded through MonthBudgetOptions/visibleCategoriesFilter; template and fixed-group exclusions re-implemented inline at setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3/6/12MonthAvg and copyPreviousMonth (which also lacks the new flag)
